welcome.description: AI-native security operations assistant — threat analysis, incident response, and security orchestration
welcome.alertOperationsSuggestion:
Help me configure the SOC workspace alert operations capability. Please proceed in order:

1. First confirm whether the FlocksHub component `soc-workspace` is installed. If it is not installed, ask me whether to install the Alert Operations Suite. If I decline, stop. If I confirm, install the component.
2. After the component is installed, read `~/.flocks/plugins/workflows/stream_alert_denoise/guide.md` and guide me through the denoise workflow configuration. Focus on Syslog settings, whether the Syslog listener should be enabled, and whether the corresponding security device is configured and sending Syslog data.
3. Then read `~/.flocks/plugins/workflows/stream_alert_triage/guide.md` and guide me through the triage workflow configuration. Focus on whether output should be DB or JSONL, and ask whether to enable scheduled triggering. The default schedule is every 5 minutes.
4. After both workflows are confirmed, tell me the SOC workspace capability is configured and can be modified later if needed.

Ask only one key question at a time, and show a plan and impact summary before changing configuration.

rea.installPrompt:
REA installation guide
Principle: install only the missing components; run everything that can run in parallel at the same time instead of waiting step by step.

1. Choose the install tier
Light tier: for JavaScript / .NET / archive analysis only. It does not install JDK or Ghidra, which saves about 1.2 GB of disk space and about 4 minutes of install time.
Full tier: for decompiling native ELF / PE. It adds JDK 21 and Ghidra 12.1.4 on top of the light tier.
2. Install the missing components in parallel (the three items below run at the same time)
Skill: source github:zouineoualid/rea-reverse-engineering/reverse-engineer-anything; the source is intermittently unreachable, so retry it as is when it fails.
JDK 21: run dnf install -y java-21-openjdk-devel.
Ghidra 12.1.4: download through the https://ghfast.top/ mirror (the official host runs at about 30 KB/s, about 4 hours); verify the official SHA-256 (ddac49f903da9d5bac833e5cc79395098b9c33cfd3279be5f31bd00387d2d4db) after downloading, discard and download again if it does not match, and unpack to /opt once it matches.
3. Register the MCP service only once
Service name rea, start command npx -y rea-agents@6.4.0 --mcp (the version must stay pinned to 6.4.0); set the environment variables GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=/opt/ghidra_12.1.4_PUBLIC and JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk. The light tier writes no environment variables.
Do not register it once before and once after installing, which only adds service reconnects.

4. Validate that it really works
Validate according to the chosen tier; a started service or the tool count (170) alone does not prove it is usable.
Light tier: no JDK/Ghidra. Use a minimal JavaScript file, a .NET managed assembly and a ZIP archive generated locally, or from a known source with their source code, and validate them with real tool calls; no analysis material from the user is needed. The JavaScript and .NET samples each contain a checkable calculation with a fixed input and output: recover the logic with the actual tools and, where possible, run it in the matching runtime; the ZIP sample contains known folders and files: list, extract and check its contents with the actual tools. Use tool names from the real MCP tool list. Report passed, failed and unfinished items one by one; some capabilities passing does not mean all of them work.
Full tier: first complete the light-tier validation, then a real native decompilation. Compile a C program of about 10 lines with a separate calculation function, call open_binary and then procedure_pseudo_code, check that the recovered logic matches the source, and run the original program to check the fixed input and output. The tool count (170) alone does not prove native decompilation works.

5. Other requirements
Reuse components that already exist; /opt/ghidra_* and /root/.npm/_npx are caches, do not delete them; keeping them cuts a repeated install from about 6 minutes to about 30 seconds.
Ask for confirmation before installing system packages or writing platform configuration.
Before installing, confirm with me again which modules you plan to install.
